options.name: control-token
options.setting-help: require a token on control connections: the client authenticates with {"cmd": "auth", "token":...}; over the unix socket a trusted peer (root, the daemon's own user or --control-trust-uids — SO_PEERCRED) skips the token (`file:<path>` = the token from an owner-only file)
options.help: require a token on control connections: the client authenticates with {"cmd": "auth", "token":...}; over the unix socket a trusted peer (root, the daemon's own user or --control-trust-uids — SO_PEERCRED) skips the token; the value may be `file:<path>` — the first line of an owner-only 0600 file (a systemd LoadCredential rides as file:/run/credentials/...)

options.name: control-ops-token
options.setting-help: a second, read-only control token: sessions authenticating with it may run the show/clear verbs only (no set/unset, no poll now, no request reload, no restart, no shutdown) — the ops shift against the admin key, both audited (`file:<path>` = the token from an owner-only file)

options.name: control-trust-uids
options.setting-help: extra peer uids the unix control socket trusts without the token (SO_PEERCRED — a local systemd unit speaks without the secret); root and the daemon's own user are always trusted

options.name: dump
options.setting-help: the state dump: the live overrides' file, the restore-on-start

options.name: dump-path
options.setting-help: the state dump file: the live overrides, written on request dump and the graceful shutdown
options.help: the state dump: the live setting overrides (the poll plan, the caps, the log surface — the tokens apart) as one JSON, written 0600 with an integrity hash (a restore refuses a tampered, unsigned or group-writable dump); dumped on the request dump command and the graceful shutdown; loaded on start only with --restore-on-start, on demand with the request restore command

options.name: dump-key
options.setting-help: the key that seals the state dumps (the reload's state file too) (`file:<path>` reads an owner-only file)
options.help: the key that seals the state dumps and the reload's state file: the state rides encrypted (an HMAC-SHA256 counter-mode keystream, authenticated — a restore refuses a wrong or missing key, and a configured key refuses an unsealed dump); the reload re-exec re-resolves the same key, so the state file reads on the other side; no key = the dumps stay 0600 plaintext with the integrity hash a dump path without a key warns at start and on set; the value may be `file:<path>` — the first line of an owner-only 0600 file (a systemd LoadCredential rides as file:/run/credentials/...)

options.name: restore-on-start
options.setting-help: the dump loads on start (off: on demand with request restore)
options.help: load the state dump when the daemon starts (needs --dump-path) — the live overrides ride again instead of a cold start; without it the dump loads on demand

commands.name: request-restart
